content: For patients receiving continuous parenteral nutrition, insulin is frequently incorporated directly into the parenteral nutrition solution. The dosage of insulin is carefully adjusted according to the patient’s blood glucose levels to maintain glycemic control. In cases where the administration of the parenteral nutrition solution is interrupted, specific adjustments must be made to avoid the risk of hypoglycemia. Additionally, if blood glucose levels increase during this interruption, corrective insulin may need to be administered separately to manage hyperglycemia effectively.
